404.text: No, ma'am. But I cleaned hospital rooms for two years while I was in school. Nothing is dirtier than a hospital.

405.text: Laundry, upstairs bedrooms, kitchen when the cook is off. Three rules. Never enter Mr. Caldwell's study. Never touch anything on his desk. And never, ever argue with Miss Pierce.

407.text: You've burned your tongue three mornings in a row, sir. A man who runs three hundred trucks should be able to wait one minute for coffee.

409.text: No. Don't be sorry. It's refreshing.

410.text: You again. The girl from the gate. Get these upstairs. Carefully. Some of those cost more than you make in a year.

411.text: Baby! You're home early. Nothing, she just didn't clean the table properly.

412.text: You men never notice anything. Come on, I want to show you the wedding flowers.

413.text: Your little brother. The inhaler. Three hundred and forty dollars, isn't it? I hear everything in this house. One word to Ethan and you'll never work in Nashville again. Understood?

415.text: I'm sorry, sir, I'm on my break, I—

416.text: Grace. Relax. You're studying physical therapy?

418.text: Because my daddy had a stroke when I was twelve. Nobody came to help him walk again. So I did. He walked me to the bus every day for six years after that.

402.text: Is it that obvious you're new?

406.text: If anybody gives you a hard time, you tell Mrs. Hayes. And if Mrs. Hayes gives you a hard time... you're on your own.

301.text: End of the month, Rick. I told you. You'll have every dollar.

302.text: Vitamins. For my brother. He works too hard. And you didn't hear any of that, sweetheart. Did you?

303.text: I know, Mama. Three hundred and forty for Sam's inhaler. I'll have it Friday.
